nodes.summary: Let $m, n \ge 1$ and let $F_0, F_1, F_2, \dots$ be the $m$-step Fibonacci numbers: $F_0 = 1$, $F_k = 2^{k-1}$ for $1 \le k \le m - 1$, and $F_k = F_{k-1} + F_{k-2} + \dots + F_{k-m}$ for $k \ge m$. Then for every binary keyword $a$ of length $m + 1$, the number of equivalence classes of the relation $\sim_a$ on binary words of length $n$ is $F_0 + F_1 + \dots + F_n$.
nodes.title: Keyword classes are counted by partial sums of $m$-step Fibonacci numbers

nodes.summary: Let $a$ and $b$ be binary keywords of length $m + 1$. The relations $\sim_a$ and $\sim_b$ have the same number of one-element equivalence classes on binary words of length $n$ for every $n \ge 0$ if and only if, for every $i$ with $1 \le i \le m + 1$, the following holds for $a$ exactly when it holds for $b$: the prefix of length $i$ of the keyword equals its suffix of length $i$ or the letterwise negation of that…
nodes.title: Keywords with equally many singleton classes

nodes.summary: Let $a$ be a binary keyword of length $m + 1$, let $n$ and $i$ be natural numbers with $i < n$, and for each index $k$ let $\varphi_k$ be the simple map of $a$ at letter $k$ on binary words of length $n$. Let $l = [j_1, \dots, j_r]$ be a list of indices that are all greater than $i$, and let $\varphi_l = \varphi_{j_r} \circ \dots \circ \varphi_{j_1}$ be the map that applies $\varphi_{j_1}$ first. Suppose that…
nodes.title: Parity of the smallest index in a non-commuting list

nodes.summary: For a binary keyword $a$, an index $j$ and a binary word $u$, the one-element list $[j]$ acts completely on $u$ if and only if the simple map $\varphi_j$ of $a$ changes $u$, that is, $\varphi_j(u) \ne u$.
nodes.title: Complete action of a one-element list

nodes.summary: Let $a$ be a binary keyword and $u$ a binary word. A list $[j_1, \dots, j_r]$ of indices acts completely on $u$ when applying the simple maps $\varphi_{j_1}, \varphi_{j_2}, \dots, \varphi_{j_r}$ of $a$ in this order changes the word at every step: with $u_0 = u$ and $u_q = \varphi_{j_q}(u_{q-1})$, we have $u_q \ne u_{q-1}$ for $1 \le q \le r$. In particular the empty list acts completely on every word.
nodes.title: Lists of simple maps acting completely

nodes.summary: Let $a = a_0 a_1 \cdots a_m$ be a binary keyword of length $m + 1$ and $u = u_0 u_1 \cdots u_{n-1}$ a binary word of length $n$. The keyword $a$ is applicable to $u$ at the ($0$-indexed) letter $i$ when $i + m < n$ and the subword $u_i u_{i+1} \cdots u_{i+m}$ of $u$ equals $a$ or the letterwise negation of $a$.
nodes.title: Applicability of a keyword

nodes.summary: Let $a$ be a binary keyword, let $u$ and $v$ be binary words of length $n$, and let $w$ be a binary word of length $n'$. Writing $xy$ for the concatenation of words $x$ and $y$, we have $u \sim_a v$ if and only if $uw \sim_a vw$, and $u \sim_a v$ if and only if $wu \sim_a wv$.
nodes.title: Keyword equivalence is stable under concatenation

nodes.summary: For every binary keyword $a$ and every binary word $u$, we have $u \sim_a u$: the empty composition of simple maps sends $u$ to itself.
nodes.title: Reflexivity of keyword equivalence

nodes.summary: Let $a$ be a binary keyword of length $m + 1$. Two binary words $u$ and $v$ of length $n$ satisfy $u \sim_a v$ when some finite composition of simple maps of $a$, possibly the empty composition, sends $u$ to $v$.
nodes.title: Keyword equivalence of binary words

nodes.summary: Let $a$ be a binary keyword and let $u$ and $v$ be binary words of length $n$. Then $u$ and $v$ are adjacent in the graph $\mathcal{G}_n^{(a)}$ if and only if $u \ne v$ and some simple map $\varphi_i$ of $a$ sends $u$ to $v$ or sends $v$ to $u$.
nodes.title: Adjacency in the keyword substitution graph

nodes.summary: Let $a$ and $b$ be keywords of length $m + 1$, and write $\varphi_i^{(a)}$ and $\varphi_i^{(b)}$ for the simple maps of $a$ and $b$ at letter $i$ on binary words of length $n$. Let $f$ be a bijection of the set of binary words of length $n$ and $\sigma$ a permutation of the positions $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$, and suppose that $f(\varphi_i^{(a)}(u)) = \varphi_{\sigma(i)}^{(b)}(f(u))$ for every word $u$ and every…
nodes.title: Intertwining bijections preserve distances in the substitution graph

nodes.summary: For every keyword $a$ of length $m + 1$ and every $n \ge 0$, the substitution graph $\mathcal{G}_n^{(a)}$ on binary words of length $n$ is bipartite.
nodes.title: The substitution graph is bipartite

nodes.summary: Let $a = a_0 a_1 \cdots a_m$ be a keyword of length $m + 1$ and let $n \ge 0$. Write $\neg a$ for the letterwise negation of $a$, $\rho(a) = a_m a_{m-1} \cdots a_0$ for its reversal, and $\bar a$ for its seminegation, which keeps $a_t$ for even $t$ and negates $a_t$ for odd $t$. Then the substitution graphs satisfy $\mathcal{G}_n^{(a)} = \mathcal{G}_n^{(\neg a)}$, and $\mathcal{G}_n^{(a)}$ is isomorphic both to…
nodes.title: Keyword symmetries of the substitution graph

nodes.summary: Let $a$ be a keyword, a binary word of length $m + 1$, and let $n \ge 0$. The substitution graph $\mathcal{G}_n^{(a)}$ is the simple graph on the binary words of length $n$ in which distinct words $u$ and $v$ are adjacent when $\varphi_i(u) = v$ or $\varphi_i(v) = u$ for some $i \in \mathbb{N}$, where $\varphi_i$ is the simple map of $a$ at letter $i$. Equivalently, $u$ and $v$ are adjacent when one is obtained…
nodes.title: Substitution graph

nodes.summary: For every keyword $a$ and every binary word $u$, applying the empty list of simple maps of $a$ to $u$ returns $u$.
nodes.title: The empty list of simple maps acts trivially

nodes.summary: Let $a$ be a keyword and, for $j \in \mathbb{N}$, let $\varphi_j$ be the simple map of $a$ at letter $j$. A list $[j_1, \dots, j_r]$ of natural numbers acts on a binary word $u$ of length $n$ by $u \mapsto \varphi_{j_r}(\cdots(\varphi_{j_1}(u))\cdots)$: the head of the list acts first, and the empty list acts as the identity.
nodes.title: Action of a list of simple maps

nodes.summary: Let $a$ be a keyword of length $m + 1$ and $u$ a binary word of length $n$, and suppose that $a$ is applicable to $u$ at letter $i$. Then the simple map $\varphi_i$ of $a$ negates the letters of $u$ at positions $i, \dots, i + m$ and leaves every other letter unchanged: for every position $j$, $\varphi_i(u)_j = \neg u_j$ if $i \le j \le i + m$, and $\varphi_i(u)_j = u_j$ otherwise.
nodes.title: An applicable simple map negates its window

nodes.summary: Let $a$ be a keyword of length $m + 1$ and let $n$ be a natural number. Let $i < j$ be natural numbers with $j + m < n$, and put $\Delta = j - i$. The simple maps $\varphi_i$ and $\varphi_j$ of $a$ on binary words of length $n$ satisfy $\varphi_i \circ \varphi_j = \varphi_j \circ \varphi_i$ if and only if $\Delta \ge m + 1$, or the prefix of $a$ of length $m + 1 - \Delta$ differs both from the suffix of $a$ of…
nodes.title: When two simple maps commute

nodes.summary: Let $a$ be a keyword and $u$ a binary word. If $a$ is not applicable to $u$ at letter $i$, then the simple map $\varphi_i$ of $a$ leaves $u$ unchanged: $\varphi_i(u) = u$.
nodes.title: A simple map that is not applicable is the identity

nodes.summary: Let $a$ be a keyword, a binary word of length $m + 1$, and let $i \in \mathbb{N}$. The simple map $\varphi_i$ sends a binary word $u$ of length $n$ to the word obtained by negating the letters of $u$ at positions $i, \dots, i + m$ (positions counted from $0$) if $a$ is applicable to $u$ at letter $i$, that is, if $i + m < n$ and the subword of $u$ at positions $i, \dots, i + m$ equals $a$ or its letterwise negation…
nodes.title: Simple map

nodes.summary: Let $m \ge 1$ and let $F : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ satisfy $F(0) = 1$, $F(k) = 2^{k-1}$ for $1 \le k \le m - 1$, and $F(k) = F(k-1) + \cdots + F(k-m)$ for $k \ge m$ (the $m$-step Fibonacci numbers). Then a real sequence $(S_n)_{n \ge 0}$ satisfies $S_n = F(0) + F(1) + \cdots + F(n)$ for all $n$ if and only if $S_n = 2^n$ for $0 \le n \le m$ and $S_n = 2 S_{n-1} - S_{n-m-1}$ for $n \ge m + 1$.
nodes.title: Recurrence for partial sums of $m$-step Fibonacci numbers

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
